basic_details.job_title: CGSSB Assistant Teacher Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Online for 2292 Posts

important_dates.correction_date: 22 August 2026 to 24 August 2026, up to 5:00 PM

application_fee.details: The application fee must be paid online at the time of filling the application form. As per Chhattisgarh Government rules, local resident candidates of Chhattisgarh who appear for the examination will get their examination fee refunded to the same bank account used for payment, after the declaration of the exam result.

exam_pattern.details: The written exam will consist of 100 objective-type (multiple choice) questions. Each question carries 1 mark. Total duration of the exam is 2 hours (10:00 AM to 12:15 PM as per admit card timing). Each question has 4 answer options; candidates must select one correct option. Negative marking is applicable: 1/4th mark will be deducted for a wrong answer or for marking more than one option for the same question. No marks (zero) will be given for unattempted questions. Answers must be marked on the OMR sheet using a black or blue ball-point pen only.

how_to_apply: Visit the official website vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in or cgssb.cgstate.gov.in.
Complete Profile Registration if you have not already registered on the portal. Once registered, candidates do not need to re-enter personal details for each individual exam application.
Upload a recent photograph with a light-coloured background, self-clicked, in .jpg/.jpeg format, with a file size between 50 KB and 100 KB.
Upload a scanned copy of your signature as a separate file, also between 50 KB and 100 KB in .jpg/.jpeg format.
Fill in the online application form for the LSAT26 exam using your registered profile details.
Pay the applicable examination fee online as per your category.
Click the "SUBMIT" button to complete the application. The application is considered complete only after clicking Submit.
Download and take a printout of the submitted application form and keep it safely for future reference.
important_instructions: Candidates must reach the exam centre at least 2 hours before the exam start time for identity verification and frisking. The main gate of the exam centre will close 30 minutes before the exam starts. Since the exam begins at 10:00 AM, the gate will close at 9:30 AM. Candidates should wear light-coloured, half-sleeve clothing. Black, dark blue, dark green, purple, maroon, and dark chocolate-coloured clothes are not allowed. Only slippers/chappals are permitted as footwear; shoes are not allowed. Wearing any type of jewellery in the ears is prohibited. Candidates in religious or cultural attire must report to the exam centre earlier than the general reporting time, as they will need to undergo an additional security check. Communication devices, electronic devices, electronic watches, purses, pouches, scarves, belts, caps, and similar items are strictly prohibited inside the exam hall. Candidates will not be allowed to leave the exam room during the first 30 minutes and the last 30 minutes of the exam. Candidates who fail to follow the instructions will be barred from appearing in the exam, and strict action will be taken against candidates found using unfair means, including cancellation of candidature.

Only candidates who fulfil the eligibility conditions specified in the departmental recruitment rules will be considered eligible; merely filling the application form or appearing in the exam does not guarantee eligibility. Caste, date of birth, local residence, educational qualification, disability, and ex-serviceman certificates are not collected at the time of application. All verification will be carried out by the recruiting appointing authority. CGSSB will not be responsible for any information provided by the candidate; the candidate is solely responsible for the accuracy of the information filled in the application. Candidates should read the recruitment rules issued by the concerned department carefully before applying and apply only if eligible. Re-checking or re-evaluation of the OMR answer sheet is not permitted, as evaluation is done through an OMR machine. CGSSB's responsibility is limited to conducting the exam and declaring the result; document verification, selection, and appointment processes are not handled by CGSSB.

Candidates preparing for teaching recruitment exams can also explore more Assistant Teacher Jobs and Chhattisgarh Government Jobs across various departments. Applicants interested in similar state-level exams can check the latest Vyapam CG Recruitment notifications and Lok Shiksha Sanchalanalaya Jobs for upcoming vacancies. Those looking for more teaching opportunities can also browse Teacher Recruitment 2026 and B.Ed/D.El.Ed Government Jobs matching their qualification.

content_sections.heading: CGSSB LSAT26 Application Correction Facility
content_sections.text: Candidates who make an error while filling the online application get 3 days after the application closing date to correct it themselves online. Basic profile corrections must first be made in the Profile Registration section; the correction will then reflect in the exam application. The result will be prepared strictly based on the information filled in by the candidate. No correction request will be entertained after this stage or at any later stage.

content_sections.heading: CGSSB Assistant Teacher Answer Key Objection Process
content_sections.text: After the exam, CGSSB will release a model answer key on its website. Candidates who disagree with the model answer key can raise objections online by logging in with their registration/profile ID and date of birth. A fee of Rs. 50/- per question must be paid online to raise an objection; objections without fee payment are not accepted. Objections sent by post, email, or submitted in person at the CGSSB office will not be accepted. Each objection must be submitted separately for each question; combined objections for multiple questions in a single submission will be rejected. All objections will be examined by subject experts, and their decision on the final answer key will be treated as final.

faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for CGSSB Sahayak Shikshak Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The online application last date is 21 August 2026 (Friday) up to 5:00 PM.

faq.question: Q2. When is the CGSSB LSAT26 exam scheduled?
faq.answer: The exam is provisionally scheduled for 11 October 2026 (Sunday), from 10:00 AM to 12:15 PM.

faq.question: Q3. What is the application fee for CGSSB Sahayak Shikshak Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The fee is Rs. 350 for General, Rs. 250 for OBC, and Rs. 200 for SC/ST/Divyang (PwD) candidates.

faq.question: Q4. Is the application fee refundable?
faq.answer: Yes, local resident candidates of Chhattisgarh who appear in the exam will get their fee refunded to the same bank account used for payment, after the result is declared.

faq.question: Q5. When will the CGSSB LSAT26 admit card be released?
faq.answer: The admit card is expected to be released on 5 October 2026 (Monday) on the official website.

faq.question: Q6. How many questions will be asked in the CGSSB Sahayak Shikshak exam?
faq.answer: The exam will have 100 objective-type questions of 1 mark each, to be solved in 2 hours.

faq.question: Q7. Is there negative marking in the CGSSB LSAT26 exam?
faq.answer: Yes, 1/4th mark will be deducted for each wrong answer or for marking multiple options for a question.

faq.question: Q8. How many exam centres are there for CGSSB Sahayak Shikshak Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The exam will be conducted at 16 district headquarters across Chhattisgarh.

faq.question: Q9. What documents are required at the exam centre?
faq.answer: Candidates must carry a printed admit card and one original photo ID such as Voter ID, Driving Licence, PAN Card, or Aadhaar Card.

faq.question: Q10. Can I make corrections in my CGSSB LSAT26 application after submission?
faq.answer: Yes, corrections can be made within 3 days after the application closing date, i.e., between 22 August 2026 and 24 August 2026.
